claims.claim: A word processor is application software for creating and editing text-based documents such as memos, letters, and reports; common examples are Microsoft Word, Google Docs, and LibreOffice/Open Office Writer.

A style is a named set of formatting attributes; applying it shifts emphasis from what text looks like to what text is, and styles provide consistency and efficiency because changing a style's definition updates every use of it.
Word processors provide several style categories (e.g., paragraph, character, page, frame, list, table styles); paragraph and heading styles carry the document's structure.
Heading styles establish document hierarchy/outline, which the software uses to generate an automatic table of contents and a navigation view.
Track changes records each user's insertions and deletions, typically in distinct colors, notes who made an edit and when, and lets the author accept or reject changes individually or all at once.
Comments flag content for feedback without altering it and can be replied to, then deleted or resolved.
Spelling and grammar check flags likely errors against a dictionary but cannot catch a correctly spelled but misused word (e.g., 'four' vs 'for'), so it aids rather than replaces proofreading.

PDF (Portable Document Format), standardized as ISO 32000, specifies a fixed-layout digital form that lets users exchange and view documents independent of the environment (software, hardware) in which they were created or viewed.
